transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I finally came in because I keep making really basic technical mistakes at work that I know better than to make. Like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third even after I’ve checked it. It’s starting to scare me.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of difficulties with attention and mistakes?
About two years, maybe two years and a couple months. It really got disruptive after the company readjustment changed the way my shoots and edit reviews were set up.
Looking back to your childhood and school years, did you ever experience similar difficulties with attention or making careless mistakes?
Yes. Even in elementary school, teachers would move my desk because I was always getting out of my seat, blurting out answers, or bothering classmates before I even realized I was doing it.
Nowadays, do you find yourself feeling restless or having difficulty sitting still for long periods?

Yes. During a client screening, sitting there quietly feels like pressure is building under my skin. I get this strong urge to stand up or do something with my body, even though I know I’m supposed to just sit and watch.
Do you notice these difficulties with focus or restlessness outside of work, such as at home or in your personal life?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid as much attention to it outside of work, I guess.
How do you manage with keeping up with daily household chores and errands at home?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really thought about whether that’s a problem for me at home.
Do you often find yourself misplacing or searching for everyday items, such as your keys, phone, or wallet?
I’m not sure, to be honest. I haven’t really noticed whether I do that more than usual.
Do you find that your mind easily wanders or that you get sidetracked by things going on around you when you're trying to focus?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether my mind wanders or if things around me distract me when I’m trying to focus.
In your daily conversations, do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are speaking?

Yeah, I do. I’ll cut into conversations before someone’s finished, especially if I think I know what they’re going to say. At work I’ve also caught myself leaning over an assistant’s shoulder and changing something on their timeline before they even asked for help. I know it can come across like I don’t trust them, which isn’t what I mean.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of inattention and technical errors at work raises differential of adult ADHD, depressive disorder, anxiety disorder, adjustment disorder, or mild cognitive impairment.
